newsitem.title: USA: Maine Yankee blames worker error for missing wire.
newsitem.headline: Maine Yankee blames worker error for missing wire.

text.p: Investigators believe the removal of a wire from a key cooling system of the Maine Yankee nuclear power plant was an accident and not sabotage, plant officials said Friday.

The 15 foot section of wire was incorrectly labled "spare" and removed between 1990 and 1992 during a project to rid the main control room circuitry of excess wires, according to plant president Charles Frizzle.

Engineers discovered the wire was missing in August during a test of pumps in the emergency core cooling system. The wire was replaced but caused Maine Yankee to extend a shutdown begun to repair a different cooling system.

A spokeswoman said repair procedures at the 24-year-old plant have been tightened as a result of the incident. The facility is back on-line, but operating at 80 percent capacity while workers replace a faulty pump on the non-nuclear side of the plant.
Maine Yankee is 38 percent owned by Central Maine Power Co, 20 percent each by New England Electric System and Northeast Utilities, and 22 percent by other New England utilities.
